item.title: Ford Workers Protest Henry Ford's Nazi Connections Dearborn, Michigan, April 1941
item.description:
During the historic Ford Motor Company strike in April 1941, workers and their families marched outside the Ford River Rouge plant in Dearborn, Michigan. In this remarkable photograph, two young boys carry protest signs questioning Henry Ford's connections to Nazi Germany. One reads, "Why did Ford get a Nazi medal?" referring to the Grand Cross of the German Eagle awarded to Ford by Nazi Germany on July 30, 1938. The strike was part of a long struggle for union recognition and better working conditions. In June 1941, Ford finally recognized the United Auto Workers (UAW). A powerful glimpse into American labor history, when even children joined their families on the picket lines. Original photograph: April 1941 Location: Dearborn, Michigan, USA Colorization: S. item.title: Wolves Descend on Finnish Villages After Google Hacked Down 1,300 Acres of Habitat to Make Room for AI Data Centers"We had wolves coming into the village because all the wild animals moved out of the forest."
item.description: Earlier in October, Finnish authorities ordered Google’s affiliate data center developer Tuike Finland Oy to immediately suspend the illegal cutting of some 1,300 acres of forest. The tech giant was given a week to draft a report explaining its actions, which soon became a flashpoint for Europe’s growing outrage over the data center boom. As the anger grew, reporters descended on the scene — and what they found is a clear-cut example of the AI revolution’s impact on the environment. New reporting by the Guardian shed fresh light on the impacts of Google’s deforestation. After the 1,300 acres of pristine boreal forests were reduced to tracts of mud and stumps, fauna which once called the woods home has been forced to vacate. In the felling-site near the Finnish village of Otanmäki, the ensuing loss of prey has forced packs of wolves to search for food elsewhere: nearby villages. “We had wolves coming into the village because all the wild animals moved out of the forest,” 53-year-old Otanmäki resident Anni Ranta told the Guardian. “They fled.” Though Ranta’s family has called the area home for generations, the tumult has her considering whether to move out of Otanmäki for good. “I don’t want them here,” she continued, speaking of Google’s data centers. “I don’t want them in Finland at all. I don’t like the whole idea of AI and the world changing and the way it’s changing. It’s going too fast, too soon.” Antti Jakonen, a resident of Muhos, put it in even starker terms. “It has been done in the wrong way. American style. No sense. No sense at all,” he told the Guardian. Sure enough, back in Google’s home country, data center developers are increasingly duking it out with the natural world — and winning handily. In West Virginia, a grove of critically endangered Chestnut trees is under threat of being bulldozed to make way for a new Anthropic hyperscale facility. Outside of Fort Wayne, a chunk of Indiana’s once-bountiful wetlands is being tilled to fit a new Google data center. In Southern New Jersey, a data center operator was recently slapped with a $1 million fine after inspectors uncovered 62 illegal gas generators belching exhaust into the surrounding environment. Wherever in the world data centers go up, it seems the destruction of natural resources is inevitable — and increasingly difficult for humanity to ignore. https://futurism.com/future-society/wolves-finland-google-ai-data-centers

item.description: New Matter-Antimatter Imbalance Model Oktay Yürük aka Oktay74tn, science and tech content https://imgur.com/user/Oktay74tn The universe's age is estimated at 13.8 billion years. This diagram shows the phases of its evolution. One open question in physics is the matter-antimatter imbalance, known as baryon asymmetry. According to a new model, neutrinos could explain why there is so much more matter than antimatter. Neutrinos are the second most abundant particles in the universe (photons no. 1). Their upper mass limit is 8 times 10 to the minus 37 kilograms. That is less than one-millionth the mass of an electron. Neutrinos barely interact with matter. They oscillate between three different flavors (electron neutrino - muon neutrino - tau neutrino). This is the discovery image of neutrinos in a hydrogen bubble chamber. The new model is based on sterile neutrinos, hypothetical particles with right-handed chirality. According to the Standard Model, neutrinos are left-handed. Antineutrinos are right-handed with their spin pointing along the direction of travel. N3 is a hypothetical, heavier right-handed neutrino. The scale factor a is dimensionless. It describes the expansion of the universe. This diagram shows the change of energy densities as a function of the relative scale factor. The radiation dominated (RD) era was temporarily ended by the N3 dominated era. The half-life of the heavy neutrinos is relatively long. When heavy anti-matter decayed, the by-products warmed up the universe. Some of the antimatter particles were annihilated. That created the matter-antimatter imbalance. The N3 dominated era ended with the decay of the N3 neutrinos. In this artist’s impression of the Milky Way, the dark matter halo is shown in blue. Dark matter outweighs bright matter by a factor of more than five. N3 neutrinos could have imapcted dark matter production and evolution. item.title: Slave trade
item.description: https://www.reddit.com/r/BlackHistoryPhotos/s/pkgXtGnnoQ https://en.rattibha.com/thread/1667928320657309696 In Louisiana, black women were put in cells with male prisoners and some became pregnant. All children born in the penitentiary to blacks were property of the state. At 10 years, they would be auctioned off. The proceeds were used to fund schools for white children. -THREAD- Before the Civil War, most prisoners in the South were white. The punishment of enslaved African Americans was generally left up to their owners. Louisiana, however, did imprison enslaved people for "serious" crimes, generally involving acts of rebellion against the slave system. A number of these imprisoned slaves were women. Penitentiary records show a number of women imprisoned for "assaulting a white," arson, or attempting to poison someone, most likely their enslavers. Some of these female prisoners became pregnant, either by fellow inmates or prison officials. In 1848, state legislatures passed a law declaring that all children born in the penitentiary to African Americans serving life sentences would become property of the state. The women would raise the children inside the prison until the age of 10, at which point they would be auctioned on the courthouse steps. Many of the buyers were prison officials, including heads of the company that ran the penitentiary. The proceeds were used to fund schools for white children. To read more on the Louisiana prison system between 1801-1861: digital.library.adelaide.edu.au
